# Marky v1.4.0

This release is mostly about the MCP server, which is published separately as
[`@marky-app/mcp-server@1.2.0`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@marky-app/mcp-server).
The desktop app itself changes only in the AI & MCP settings panel.

### Security

- **Vault containment for the MCP server.** `create_note` accepted a `folder` argument containing `..` and wrote outside the vault. Because that argument is chosen by a model, a note carrying injected instructions could have steered a write anywhere the user can write. Every write now resolves against the vault root and is refused if it escapes, and an absolute folder is treated as vault-relative rather than as a filesystem path.
- **Read-only mode.** Run the server with `--read-only` (or `MARKY_READ_ONLY=1`) to expose only the read tools and refuse every write.
- **Guarded overwrites.** `update_note` replaces a whole file. It now accepts `expected_hash` from a previous `read_note` and refuses the write if the note changed in between, so an AI rewrite can no longer silently discard an edit you made in the app.

### Fixed

- **Daily notes now match the app.** The server wrote `Daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md` while the app writes `YYYY-MM-DD.md` at the vault root, so the app and an AI client created two unrelated notes for the same day and `daily_review` found nothing for real vaults. The server now writes where the app does. Notes created by earlier versions under `Daily/` are still found, appended to, and included in reviews — no migration needed.
- **`search_notes` ignored its `limit`.** A schema ordering mistake made the default resolve to nothing, so every search returned its full result set.
- **`list_notes` was unbounded.** On a 2,000-note vault a single response serialised roughly 75k tokens, enough to exhaust a model's context on its own. It is now paginated and reports a `total`.
- **Note lookup no longer matches across a name boundary**, so `Note.md` cannot resolve to `MyNote.md`.

### Performance

The vault index was rebuilt from disk on every call, and `read_note` built it twice. Measured on 2,000 notes: a cold read halves from 4,000 file reads to 2,000, repeat calls do no disk I/O at all, and changing one note re-reads exactly that one file.

### MCP protocol

- Every tool now carries annotations, so clients can auto-approve reads separately from writes. Six tools are marked read-only; `update_note` is marked destructive.
- Every tool declares an `outputSchema` and returns `structuredContent`, so results can be consumed as typed JSON rather than re-parsed from text.
- Resources gained descriptions and a listing callback, so individual notes are discoverable instead of guessable.
- Added server instructions, `--version`, and graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM.

**Breaking for anyone parsing tool output directly:** structured output must be a JSON object, so `search_notes` now returns `{ query, returned, results }` and `get_tags` returns `{ tags }` instead of bare arrays.

### App

- The AI & MCP settings panel uses inline icons in place of emoji, and its status badge now reads "No workspace" when no vault is open rather than claiming readiness.

### Internal

- The MCP server package had no working test configuration and its suite had never run. It now has one, and 30 tests covering vault containment, result limits, the daily-note contract, concurrent-edit refusal, and every tool's declared output schema.
